findings.title: Hard 450-line cap violated: the modified cli_help.rs is 481 lines
findings.evidence: `git show :crates/clio-lib/src/cli_help.rs | wc -l` -> 481 (HEAD: 446; staged diff adds 35 lines); `wc -l crates/clio-lib/src/cli_help.rs` -> 481. The developer run log (private/clio-private/runs/phase-100376/developer-task-r1.log line 6) claims 'all Rust files <=450 lines', which is false for this file. All other created/modified Rust files are <=450 (largest new file: cli_write_portability_tests.rs, 444).
findings.requirement_ref: Developer task hard rules ('Every Rust file you create or modify stays at or below 450 total lines'); AGENTS.md 'Source File Size Constraint'; gaps/full-cli.md §9 ('Estimate size before adding to a near-limit file; split first')
findings.recommendation: Split cli_help.rs (for example move VERB_USAGE or the binding table into a sibling cli_help_bindings.rs) so every created/modified Rust file is <=450 lines, then re-run make check and make coverage; correct the run-log and phase-file claims accordingly.
findings.resolution: Split the usage table out of cli_help.rs into a new sibling crates/clio-lib/src/cli_help_usage.rs (VERB_USAGE + usage_for); cli_help.rs::verb_help now calls cli_help_usage::usage_for. Line counts after: cli_help.rs 262, cli_help_usage.rs 241 (both <=450); a wc -l scan over git diff --name-only + untracked shows no changed/new Rust file >450. Scoped tests: `cargo test -p clio --bin clio` -> 480 passed. Coverage (make coverage): cli_help.rs 100.00% lines/100.00% funcs, cli_help_usage.rs 100.00%/100.00%. make check green.

findings.title: Canonical dry-run-then-confirm hygiene clean fails cross-process (UNIQUE batch id), yet AC-100376-01 records PASS
findings.evidence: Fresh temp DB, two processes: `./target/debug/clio hygiene clean --file c3.json --action discard --bank demo --db /tmp/opencode/adv-cli/clio3.db` -> exit 0, {"dry_run":true,"would_discard":1}; then `... --confirm --reason noise ...` -> exit 1, {"code":"internal","message":"hygiene log insert: UNIQUE constraint failed: hygiene_audit_logs.id"}, while `stats` shows items_active 0 (the discard persisted). A confirm with no preceding dry-run succeeds (exit 0). Root cause: the clean batch id comes from a per-process counter that restarts every process (crates/clio-mcp/src/hygiene_tools.rs:92 `batch_id: &format!("hclean-{}", state.next_item_id())`; crates/clio-mcp/src/runtime_context.rs:35-41). The dry-run path persists durable `dry_run:true` log rows (confirmed live via `clio hygiene log`), whose ids collide with the confirmed insert. Phase file line 231 (AC-100376-01) labels the flow PASS and does not state the confirm exit code; line 255 (limitation 2) discloses the abort but no owning phase is named.
findings.requirement_ref: phase-100376 §8 T100376-03, §9 AC-100376-01; §12 Known Limitations; developer task 'Known limitations state ... which phase owns the debt'
findings.recommendation: Qualify AC-100376-01 with the observed exit 1 and name the owning phase/track for the id-generation defect; remediate by making the clean batch id collision-free (store-derived or invocation-unique) in the phase that owns hygiene/MCP runtime semantics, with a cross-process regression test (fresh process dry-run -> confirm).
findings.resolution: Added McpState::next_clean_batch_id (crates/clio-mcp/src/runtime_context.rs) mixing process id + nanosecond clock + in-process counter; hygiene_tools.rs binds batch_id to it. Regression test hygiene_clean_dry_run_then_confirm_across_fresh_runtime_instances opens two fresh McpState instances over one file-backed SQLite DB (fresh state restarts the counter, like a fresh process): dry-run then confirm both return ok:true, applied:["xproc-1"]. On the old id both states produce hclean-itm-mcp-0, so the dry-run row hlg-hclean-itm-mcp-0-0-xproc-1 collides and the confirm insert fails UNIQUE. Scoped: `cargo test -p clio-mcp hygiene` -> 12 passed; coverage hygiene_tools.rs 99.22%/100%, runtime_context.rs 100%/100%. make check + make coverage green.

findings.title: The 'run standalone' expected outcome is not true for audit/export/import over durable data (in-process LocalDevKms)
findings.evidence: Live against a temp file DB whose item was written by an earlier CLI process: `./target/debug/clio hygiene audit --bank demo --db /tmp/opencode/adv-cli/clio.db` -> exit 1, {"code":"forbidden","message":"no DEK for subject `itm-cli-737432800-592671`"}; `./target/debug/clio export --out bundle.json --actor harness --bank demo --db /tmp/opencode/adv-cli/clio.db` -> exit 1, same error; no bundle file written. Root cause is the fresh in-process `LocalDevKms` opened per CLI process (crates/clio-mcp/src/runtime.rs:244). The phase file discloses this as limitation 1 (lines 254 and 250) and earlier phases recorded the same pre-existing limitation; AC-100376-01/02 rows label PASS while their live-capable paths are clean/erase gates and in-process tests only.
findings.requirement_ref: phase-100376 §1 Expected Outcome ('run standalone'), §9 AC-100376-01/02; gaps/full-cli.md §10 items 1-2; FR-29/FR-33
findings.recommendation: Keep the disclosure but add the cross-process caveat to the AC-100376-01/02 rows and surface it at the point of failure (help or error hint: content written by another process needs a durable KMS provider); assign the durable DEK provider to a named phase/track so the debt has an owner.
findings.resolution: A durable DEK/KMS provider is out of scope (this phase must not change the DEK/erase mechanism), so resolved by disclosure + failure-point surfacing. AC-100376-01/02 now carry the cross-process KMS caveat; limitation 1 names the owning track (DEK/KMS persistence track) and records that no roadmap phase is currently assigned (pre-existing unassigned debt, first recorded in the Phase 100370 CLI phase). The CLI now attaches an actionable hint at the failure point: cross_process_dek_hint in cli_error.rs keys on `no DEK for subject` and adds `the default key provider is process-local; content written by another process needs a durable KMS provider`; call_tool applies it. Test tool_failure_adds_the_cross_process_dek_hint; cli_error.rs coverage 100%/100%.

findings.title: Confirmed clean reports a per-item failure as exit 0 and hides it from the text view
findings.evidence: Live: re-running `./target/debug/clio hygiene clean --file c2.json --action discard --confirm --reason noise --bank demo --db /tmp/opencode/adv-cli/clio2.db` on an already-discarded target -> exit 0 with {"applied":[],"failed":{"error":"invalid_argument: item `itm-cli-...` is already discarded", ...}}; `--output text` prints only 'hygiene clean: applied 0 item(s)' (no failed target, no error, no pending detail). Code: crates/clio-lib/src/cli_write_hygiene.rs:210-231 renders applied/pending but never `failed`; crates/clio-lib/src/cli_write_hygiene.rs:71-74 refuses nothing; crates/clio-lib/src/cli_write.rs:156-169 returns exit 0 for any ok payload. The developer's own batch-abort test (cli_write_hygiene_tests.rs:251-275) asserts exit 0 for a 1-applied/1-pending partial batch.
findings.requirement_ref: phase-100376 §9 AC-100376-01 ('Candidates actioned'); gaps/full-cli.md §5 items 2 and 5 (actionable typed errors, exit-code contract)
findings.recommendation: Render the failed target and its error plus the pending count in the text view, and either map a batch abort to exit 1 / a refusal or document partial-success exit 0 explicitly in the help; add a golden text-output test for the failure path.
findings.resolution: render_clean now prints the failing target and its error plus the pending count (`hygiene clean: applied 1 item(s); failed itm-ghost (…); aborted, 1 pending`), and the new WriteGroup::failure_exit seam makes a confirmed batch abort exit 1 while the JSON payload still carries applied/failed/pending. Golden tests: clean_reports_a_confirmed_batch_abort_in_text (exit 1, text) and clean_confirmed_batch_abort_exits_one_with_json_detail. Coverage cli_write_hygiene.rs 96.47%/95.24%. make check green.

findings.title: hygiene audit text view silently drops the scan-budget 'incomplete' signal
findings.evidence: crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read_hygiene.rs:129-131 renders only 'hygiene audit (bank X): scanned N active items, M candidates'; the tool marks banks larger than the scan budget via `incomplete` (crates/clio-hygiene/src/audit.rs:70-73) and the JSON payload carries it, but text users get no truncation notice. gaps/full-cli.md §5 item 6 requires bounded output to never silently truncate hygiene_audit.
findings.requirement_ref: gaps/full-cli.md §5 item 6; phase-100376 §4 Discovery (hygiene_audit partial scan)
findings.recommendation: Append a '(partial scan: bank exceeds the scan budget)' marker to the audit text summary when `incomplete` is true, with a text-render test.
findings.resolution: render_audit appends ` (partial scan: bank exceeds the scan budget)` when the tool payload's `incomplete` flag is true; a complete scan is unchanged. Test audit_text_marks_a_partial_scan covers true and false. Coverage cli_read_hygiene.rs 99.19%/100%.

findings.title: hygiene clean rejects --dry-run although the CLI-wide UX contract promises it on every mutation
findings.evidence: `./target/debug/clio hygiene clean --dry-run --file /tmp/opencode/adv-cli/cands.json --db /tmp/opencode/adv-cli/clio.db` -> exit 2, unknown flag (the group spec at crates/clio-lib/src/cli_write_hygiene.rs:45-47 lists file/action/reason/note/confirm only). The unconfirmed call is the implicit dry-run and the help says so, but gaps/full-cli.md §5 item 4 and §10 item 3 promise `--dry-run` on every mutation.
findings.requirement_ref: gaps/full-cli.md §5 item 4, §10 item 3; phase-100376 §5 Implementation Freedom (help wording)
findings.recommendation: Accept `--dry-run` on hygiene clean as an explicit alias that forces the unconfirmed dry-run path, or record the deviation in the phase file's Known Limitations.
findings.resolution: HygieneWriteGroup::spec now accepts --dry-run; clean_call forces the unconfirmed zero-write path when --dry-run is present even with --confirm/--yes; the per-command usage line (cli_help_usage.rs) and clio help catalog (main.rs) updated. Test clean_dry_run_flag_forces_zero_writes_even_with_confirm -> exit 0, dry_run:true, would_discard:1, stats items_active unchanged; spec test asserts the flag.
